verdict.rationale: JumpCloud's own docs list hardware keys, biometric and JumpCloud Go (described as hardware-protected, phishing-resistant passwordless login) as MFA methods beyond push and TOTP, and say MFA can be enforced across SAML/OIDC apps. However, the evidence never names FIDO2/WebAuthn or passkeys explicitly. It also never shows a policy that requires a specific phishing-resistant factor for selected sensitive apps; the conditional-access evidence covers only network and device-compliance conditions. missing for 10: explicit FIDO2/passkey naming, documented per-app policy requiring phishing-resistant factors, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, MFA goes beyond push codes — FIDO2 security keys and passkeys are supported and can be REQUIRED by policy for sensitive apps

citations.quote: choose from push-based, time-based one time passwords (TOTP), JumpCloud Go, hardware keys, biometric, certificates, or other methods
Pair with JumpCloud Go™ for a hardware-protected and phishing-resistant MFA passwordless login method for users to access web resources from managed devices.
Enforce SSO and multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all SAML and OIDC-based apps.
